newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply up on Clinton win.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply up on Clinton win.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures shook off their recent pessimism and shot to a firm finish on Wednesday on euphoria over President Bill Clinton's election victory and the Republican sweep of Congressional races.

Dealers said the market received an early lift from news Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had been successfully completed and extended its gains on the back of the U.S. election results.

"There were a lot of buying orders coming in at the open. And people were afraid to sell because of all the good news," said a trader with a Japanese futures house, adding that the market was not expecting a change in U.S. policy towards Japan.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract ended 80 points above the key 21,000 level against a previous settlement at 20,640. It tested a high of 21,140.
"The results came in as expected and that's friendly for U.S. business," said a trader with a local institution.
"This is a good recovery but the market's close below the 21,130 level indicates it's still consolidating," he added.
The December Nikkei would need to close above 21,130 to see further gains and above 21,300 to negate its recent downtrend, he said.
Dealers said players were likely to be somewhat cautious ahead of the formation of a new Japanese cabinet on Thursday.
